references.text: The first teruah blast as a signal for the camps on the east side to break camp, which is the direct context for the second blast in verse 6.
Describes the two silver trumpets that were to be used to assemble the congregation and give signals for breaking camp.
Describes the camp arrangement for the tribes located to the south (the camp of Reuben), who were to break camp at the second teruah blast.
The actual execution of the departure for the camp of Reuben (the southern side) as the second in sequence.
The teruah sound from horns at Jericho, illustrating the use of alarm signals in an Israelite context.
Teruah is mentioned in connection with the festival of the seventh month, showing the significance of this signal in Israel's worship.
